## Ordering FLOAT64 values
# Expected values follow the documentation's order of floating point values, from least to
# greatest: NULL, NaN, -inf, finite values and +inf.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types.md

SELECT ARRAY_AGG(id ORDER BY x) FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 1.0 AS x), (2, CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)), (3, CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)), (4, CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)), (5, NULL), (6, -2.0)])
=> [{"v":"5"},{"v":"2"},{"v":"3"},{"v":"6"},{"v":"1"},{"v":"4"}]

SELECT ARRAY_AGG(id ORDER BY x NULLS LAST) FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 1.0 AS x), (2, CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)), (3, CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)), (4, CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)), (5, NULL), (6, -2.0)])
=> [{"v":"2"},{"v":"3"},{"v":"6"},{"v":"1"},{"v":"4"},{"v":"5"}]

SELECT ARRAY_AGG(id ORDER BY x DESC) FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 1.0 AS x), (2, CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)), (3, CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)), (4, CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)), (5, NULL), (6, -2.0)])
=> [{"v":"4"},{"v":"1"},{"v":"6"},{"v":"3"},{"v":"2"},{"v":"5"}]

SELECT ARRAY_AGG(id ORDER BY x DESC NULLS FIRST) FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 1.0 AS x), (2, CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)), (3, CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)), (4, CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)), (5, NULL), (6, -2.0)])
=> [{"v":"5"},{"v":"4"},{"v":"1"},{"v":"6"},{"v":"3"},{"v":"2"}]

SELECT id FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 1.0 AS x), (2, CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)), (3, CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)), (5, NULL)]) ORDER BY x LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
=> "2"

SELECT id FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 1.0 AS x), (2, CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)), (3, CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)), (5, NULL)]) ORDER BY x DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2
=> "2"

SELECT r FROM (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY x) AS r FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 1.0 AS x), (2, CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)), (3, CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64))])) WHERE id = 2
=> "1"

# Values in a cumulative RANGE frame, which has no offset: NaN precedes -inf.
SELECT n FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY x RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS n FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 1.0 AS x), (2, CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64)), (3, CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64))])) WHERE id = 3
=> "2"
